topic: Qwen Q4_K_M, Bonsai quality verdict, measured bandwidth, wrap-up/unwrap skills

measured_bandwidth.note: card reaches full spec bandwidth; clock ramp is not the bottleneck

qwen_ud_q4_k_m.ppl_verdict: indistinguishable from Q6_K; Bonsai PQ2_0 is 3.8833 (27.5% worse)

mtp_vulkan_262k_q8q4_mmproj.note: n4 optimal; high-50s/60s not reachable with the built-in MTP head

qwen_ud_q4_k_m.conclusion: Q4_K_M is the better default: same quality, +35% unspeculated decode, 6.5 GiB less VRAM. MTP speed is similar to Q6_K.

bonsai_quality_verdict.finding: vendor average excludes agentic coding: SWE-bench Verified 60.8 vs 80.6 (~75.4%), Terminal-Bench 2.1 52.8 vs 69.7 (~75.8%). Independent reproduction absent. HF community reports poor coding and broken tool calling.

measured.suites: code/math/instruct/extract/research/tools all tied with Qwen; suites are saturated

bonsai_quality_verdict.closer_to: neither Q6_K nor Q4_K_M; ~27% worse than both on heldout perplexity
bonsai_quality_verdict.recommendation: not a replacement for Qwen; viable as a niche co-resident/Mimir backend where extraction/format/tool JSON matter, but agentic coding degrades ~25% and long-context is untested

kernel_profile.top: mul_mat_q PQ2_0 prefill GEMM 54.1% of GPU time (compute-bound); decode GEMV ~17.6%; SSM 8.7%; FWHT 2.1%

opencode_skills.note: opencode dedupes by name and the global config wins over ~/.claude/skills; verified with `opencode debug skill`
